targetText: The cleavage between "town and country," as well as the "development of this cleavage," formerly confined to one country only, are now being reproduced on a tremendously enlarged basis. Viewed from this standpoint, entire countries appear to-day as "towns," namely, the industrial countries, whereas entire agrarian territories appear to be "country."
summary: World capitalism reproduces the division between town and country on a global scale, turning industrial powers into 'towns' and agrarian colonies into 'country'.
explanation: Bukharin extends Marx's analysis of the urban-rural division of labor to the world economy, explaining how uneven capitalist development polarizes the globe into industrial manufacturing centers and dependent agricultural or extractive peripheries.
